_comment: All Adventurers Guild innkeeper dialogue. tools/EspGen turns this into dialogue records (INFO FormIDs are pinned in dialogue.ids.json, which voice files are named after - never renumber). The voice pipeline reads the same file. Keep lines short: they will be voiced.
_liaisons: The Guild keeps a counter only at the inn of each hold capital, the towns that have a Missives board. Only these innkeepers register, promote and open the counter. Optional per liaison: '<role>Ask' (their own fee ask), 'businessByRank' (business line by the player's rank: C, B, A, S; the plain 'business' line covers E-D), 'afterQuest' {quest, <role>: lines} (replaces those lines once the quest is completed). 'replace': what they say handing over a replacement guild card (the topic is only offered to a member who carries no card; the fee is in the player's line, so there is no ask). 'successor' {of, quest, alias, ref, cell}: this NPC keeps the counter once the liaison they follow is dead, whoever runs the inn (with the Unofficial Patch Mikael takes the Bannered Mare over, not Ysolda). quest + alias = the hold's Dialogue quest and its Innkeeper alias ('Plugin|0xID', number): the game swaps the backup in when the innkeeper dies, which is how the DLL knows. ref = the successor's own reference; cell = the inn: they do Guild business only there, and 'away' is what they say anywhere else. The DLL adds them to AG_GuildLiaisonFaction, and every line of theirs waits for that.

liaisons.register: Welcome to the Adventurers Guild! Here's your guild card. The Companions will sneer, but the Guild pays on time, and the work's never dull.
liaisons.business: Guild business? Pull up a stool. Saadia, mind the bar.
liaisons.promoteAsk: Let's see what the ledger says about you. Well, well! You've earned your next rank. There's just the Guild's fee to make it official.
liaisons.promote: Congratulations, love. Here's your new card; now go and eat something hot before the next job finds you. It always does.
about: Whiterun sits at the crossroads of Skyrim, so every job in the hold comes through my door first.
The Companions take the jobs that make a good song. Adventurers take the ones that need doing. Farmers know the difference.
Every stool in here had an adventurer on it, before the wars. I'd like to see that again before I hang up my apron.
liaisons.registerAsk: Looking to join the Adventurers Guild? Good, we could use new blood. There's a small fee to put your name down, that's all.

businessByRank.C: Sit, love. You've the look of someone who's walked in off the plains. Tell me the giants are still keeping to their fires.
businessByRank.B: I kept your stool by the fire. Had to turn a Battle-Born off it twice. Worth it to see his face.
businessByRank.A: The caravans ask for you by name before they'll take the north road. I tell them an adventurer like that doesn't come cheap, and they pay it.
businessByRank.S: An S-rank at the Bannered Mare. Whiterun will talk about this for a year. What can I do for you?

liaisons.replace: Lost it already? Happens to the best of them. Here, a fresh one. Try to keep this one out of the mead.

liaisons.registerAsk: Joining the Adventurers Guild? Smart. There's a small fee, and it's the best coin you'll spend this year.
liaisons.register: Welcome to the Adventurers Guild! Here's your guild card. You bring in the work, I'll see we both profit by it.
liaisons.business: Guild business? My favorite kind. What are you bringing me?

businessByRank.C: A regular! Regulars are how a merchant gets rich. What do you need?
businessByRank.B: A B-rank adventurer at my counter. You're good for trade, you know. People come in just to say they saw you.
businessByRank.A: An A-rank, at my counter! The good mead's on me. Call it an investment.
businessByRank.S: An S-rank adventurer, at my counter. I couldn't buy a sign this good. Anything you need, ask.

liaisons.promoteAsk: Let me look at your record. Oh, that's a healthy one. You've earned your next rank. There's the Guild's fee, and then it's yours.
liaisons.promote: Congratulations! I've updated your guild card. A higher rank means better-paying work. For both of us.
about: The Khajiit caravans taught me this: know what's on the road before anyone else does. Every job in the hold comes through the Bannered Mare first.
Bandits are bad for trade, and so are trolls. Every missive an adventurer finishes puts coin back in Whiterun's market.
Hulda kept this counter for years and never charged what it was worth. I mean to do right by her, and turn a profit doing it.
liaisons.replace: Lost your guild card? Replacements cost, I'm afraid. A merchant can't give away stock. Here you are.
liaisons.away: Guild business? Not out here. I keep the Adventurers Guild's counter at the Bannered Mare. Come and find me when I'm there.

liaisons.register: Welcome to the Adventurers Guild! Here's your guild card. Solitude's never short of work, and now you're first in line.
liaisons.business: Adventurers Guild business, friend? Sit, relax. Whatever chased you here stops at my doorway.
liaisons.promoteAsk: A step up? I'd say so. The East Empire clerks drink here, and they've stopped complaining about the roads. That's your doing. The Adventurers Guild asks its fee, and it's yours.
liaisons.promote: Congratulations, friend. Here's your new card. Tonight you sit, relax, and let somebody else's troubles wait at the door.
about: Solitude's the capital, so the work is as often a noble's quiet problem as a wolf on the road. Both pay. The noble pays better.
The coast north of here is wrecks, horkers and men who'd rather their cargo wasn't found. An adventurer who can keep quiet does well in Haafingar.
I've poured for adventurers who walked up the Embassy road and never came back for their change. I still have it, if they do.
liaisons.registerAsk: An adventurer wanting to sign on? Splendid! Solitude always has work for a capable blade. The Guild asks a small fee to join.

businessByRank.C: Ah, our rising star. Solitude's merchants have started asking for you by name.
businessByRank.B: The dockhands were laying wagers on what you'd bring back this time. I had my coin on you coming back at all. Easiest money I ever made.
businessByRank.A: Our A-rank! Half of Solitude wants to hire you and the other half wants to meet you. Your card?
businessByRank.S: An S-rank in the Winking Skeever. I'll have Sorex frame your signature. What do you need?

liaisons.replace: Lost your card? Careless, but easily mended. There you are, good as new.

liaisons.registerAsk: Joining the Adventurers Guild? Your funeral. There's a small fee first. There's always a fee.
liaisons.register: Welcome to the Adventurers Guild. Here's your guild card. Try not to die before your first job. It's bad for business.
liaisons.business: Guild business? Fine. Let's get it over with.

businessByRank.C: You again. Still alive, I see. What do you need?
businessByRank.B: A B-rank adventurer. My father would have fawned over you. I'll just ask what you want.
businessByRank.A: An A-rank, at the Winking Skeever. Drink's on me. Don't tell anyone, I've a reputation.
businessByRank.S: An S-rank. Huh. I didn't think I could still be impressed. What do you need?

liaisons.promoteAsk: Let's see the ledger. Well, look at that. You've earned your next rank. The Guild wants its fee first, naturally.
liaisons.promote: Congratulations. I've updated your guild card. Go on, look pleased with yourself.
about: I ran errands for the old man my whole life. Now the Winking Skeever's mine, and so is the Adventurers Guild's counter. Be careful what you wish for.
Solitude's missives are mostly wolves on the road and smugglers on the coast. Nobles pay well to have their problems go away quietly.
Half the adventurers who sign this ledger never come back to it. The other half drink here. I make coin either way.
liaisons.replace: Lost your guild card already? Of course you did. Here. That's coming out of your pocket, not mine.
liaisons.away: Not here. The Adventurers Guild's counter is at the Winking Skeever. So am I, most days.

liaisons.register: Here's your guild card. You're an adventurer now, same as the ones who tramp snow up my stairs. Wipe your boots like they don't.
liaisons.business: Come in out of the wind. If it's Adventurers Guild business, I'm listening. If it's a drink, the great room's upstairs.
liaisons.promoteAsk: Moving up, you reckon. I hear things at this bar. Carters, guards, hunters off the steam fields. They've been saying your name. That'll do me. There's the fee.
liaisons.promote: It's done. You'll find the work gets colder and the pay gets better. That's Eastmarch for you.
about: Eastmarch work is trolls on the roads and ice wraiths off the mountains. Nothin' fancy. Nothin' magic, neither, and I'll thank you to keep it so.
Come back cold and you'll get the fire, bread and a bed. Come back bleeding and you'll get the same, but you'll mop the floor after.
Half the adventurers who drank under that candle went off to the Great War. Nords died by the thousands. I still set out more bread than I've mouths for.
liaisons.registerAsk: Adventurer, is it? Eastmarch eats them. Trolls on the roads, wraiths off the ice. If you still want in, the Adventurers Guild takes a fee.

businessByRank.C: Back off the road with all your fingers. Get by the fire before you drip on my floor.
businessByRank.B: There's bread just out, and the bed on the ground floor's aired. I don't do that for everyone, so don't go telling it about.
businessByRank.A: A lad upstairs was halfway through his sabre cat story when you walked in. Stopped dead. Nobody wants to tell one in front of you.
businessByRank.S: That candle upstairs has burned a hundred and sixty-three years for one great warrior. First time I've thought it might have company.

liaisons.replace: Down a troll's gullet, I hope, and not just the back of a bed. Here's another, and it'll cost you.

liaisons.registerAsk: Looking to join the Adventurers Guild? Good for you, good for you. There's a small fee, I'm sorry to say.
liaisons.register: Welcome to the Adventurers Guild! Here's your guild card. Mind yourself out there, and come back for a hot meal.
liaisons.business: Guild business? Sit down by the fire, and we'll see to it.

businessByRank.C: There you are. I kept the stew warm. Now, what can I do for you?
businessByRank.B: A B-rank adventurer in Candlehearth Hall. Elda would never have believed it. What do you need?
businessByRank.A: An A-rank! Sit, sit. The best cut's yours tonight, no charge.
businessByRank.S: An S-rank adventurer, by my fire. I'll be telling this one till I'm in the ground. Anything you need.

liaisons.promoteAsk: Let me find my spectacles. There. Why, you've earned your next rank! There's the Guild's fee, and then it's done.
liaisons.promote: Congratulations! I've updated your guild card. I'm proud of you, I truly am.
about: I was only ever the cook. Elda kept the Adventurers Guild's counter, and now it's fallen to me. I do my best by it.
Windhelm's cold, and the work's colder. Ice wraiths, trolls on the roads. Eat before you go out.
Adventurers keep this city fed. When the roads are clear, the carts get through. People forget that.
liaisons.replace: Lost your guild card? Never mind, never mind. Here's a new one. Keep it somewhere dry.
liaisons.away: Oh, not out here. Come by Candlehearth Hall and I'll see to your Guild business there.

liaisons.register: Welcome to the Guild. Here's your card. Keep your hands out of other people's pockets and you'll do fine.
liaisons.business: Guild business. Good. At least one guild in Riften does its work in the open.
liaisons.promoteAsk: Talen, bring me the ledger. Well. You've been busy, and the Guild noticed. The fee, and the rank is yours.
liaisons.promote: Congratulations. Your guild card's updated. Try to stay alive long enough to enjoy it.
about: The Rift's got more bandits than honest folk, and the Black-Briars like it that way.
If a missive looks too easy in Riften, read it twice. Someone's usually getting paid to look away.
Adventurers have been vanishing since the war. Nobody says who's doing it. Everybody knows.
liaisons.registerAsk: You want to join the Adventurers Guild? Good. Riften needs honest blades more than most. There's a fee, of course.

businessByRank.C: Back in one piece. That's more than most manage. What's the business?
businessByRank.B: Our veteran. Talen, keep the good stuff behind the bar for this one. What do you need?
businessByRank.A: An A-rank in Riften. Even the Thieves Guild knows better than to pick your pockets. Business?
businessByRank.S: An S-rank in the Bee and Barb. Even the Black-Briars will mind their manners. Business?

liaisons.replace: Lost, or lifted? In Riften it's usually lifted. Here's a new one. Keep it somewhere your purse isn't.

liaisons.registerAsk: You wish to join the Adventurers Guild? That is good. There is a small fee, as is the custom.
liaisons.register: Welcome to the Adventurers Guild. Here is your guild card. Keerava kept this counter with care. I will do the same.
liaisons.business: Guild business? Of course. I am at your service.

businessByRank.C: You return. It is good to see a familiar face at this counter. What do you need?
businessByRank.B: A B-rank adventurer. You honor the Bee and Barb. How may I serve you?
businessByRank.A: An A-rank, in Riften. I will mix you something special. It is on the house.
businessByRank.S: An S-rank adventurer. The Hist itself must have guided you here. Ask anything of me.

liaisons.promoteAsk: Allow me to consult the ledger. Yes. You have earned your next rank. There is the Guild's fee, and then it is yours.
liaisons.promote: Congratulations. I have updated your guild card. Keerava would have been pleased.
about: This was Keerava's counter. I keep it in her memory, as I keep the Bee and Barb.
In Riften, not every job is posted on a board. The Adventurers Guild's work is honest. That is rarer here than it should be.
The Rift is full of bears, bandits and worse. An adventurer with a clear head lives longer. I will say no more about the mead.
liaisons.replace: You have lost your guild card? In Riften, check your pockets twice. Here is another.
liaisons.away: Not here. I keep the Adventurers Guild's counter at the Bee and Barb. Find me there.

liaisons.register: Welcome to the Guild. Your card, friend. Mind the Silver-Bloods, they own this inn and the Guild's rent too.
liaisons.business: Guild business, yes. Quickly now, before someone important walks in.
liaisons.promoteAsk: Let me check the ledger. You've earned your next rank, friend. Pay the fee and we'll make it official, quietly.
liaisons.promote: Congratulations. Your guild card's updated. Wear the new rank carefully in this city.
about: The Reach is Forsworn country. The Guild pays well out here, because not everyone comes back.
Anything you hear in Markarth, the Silver-Bloods heard first. Remember that.
We lost a lot of good adventurers to the wars. The ones left are the stubborn kind. That's the kind I like.
liaisons.registerAsk: Joining the Guild? Welcome, friend. Quietly now, this is the Silver-Bloods' inn. There's a small fee to sign on.

businessByRank.C: You're making a name for yourself, friend. Carefully, now. What is it?
businessByRank.B: A veteran. The Silver-Bloods have noticed you. Let's keep this quiet.
businessByRank.A: One of the Guild's finest, in Markarth. The Silver-Bloods are nervous. I rather like it. What is it?
businessByRank.S: An S-rank, here. Thonar himself asked if you'd drink with him. Business first?

liaisons.replace: Lost your card? In Markarth that's the least of what people lose. There, a new one.

liaisons.register: Welcome to the Guild. Here's your card. Falkreath has more graves than guests, so try not to add to them.
liaisons.business: Guild business. Good. Better you than the undertaker.
liaisons.promoteAsk: Let's see if the ledger has you marked for promotion or the graveyard. Promotion! Good for you. Pay the fee and I'll write it in.
liaisons.promote: Congratulations! Your guild card's updated. And you're still breathing. Rare, for Falkreath.
about: Half the missives in Falkreath end at the graveyard. The other half end there later.
The woods are thick with wolves and worse. Bring back proof of the hunt, and the Guild pays.
Falkreath's cemetery is full of adventurers from the Great War. The Guild never forgets them.
liaisons.registerAsk: Signing on with the Guild? Brave of you. Falkreath will keep you busy. There's just a small fee first.

businessByRank.C: Still breathing? Good for you. What's the business?
businessByRank.B: You've outlived most of the adventurers who drank here. Sit down. What do you need?
businessByRank.A: A-rank, and still breathing. Falkreath's never seen the like. What do you need?
businessByRank.S: An S-rank. The undertaker's going to be disappointed. What can I do for you?

liaisons.replace: Oh, you've lost it? No harm done. Here's a new card, dear.

liaisons.register: Welcome to the Guild! Here's your card. Morthal's lucky to have you.
liaisons.business: Guild business. Come closer, folk in Morthal like to listen.
liaisons.promoteAsk: Let me check the ledger. Morthal doesn't see many rise this far, but you have. There's a small fee, then it's official.
liaisons.promote: Congratulations! I've updated your guild card. Morthal's proud of you, even if it won't say so.
about: Things come out of the marsh fog that don't belong in any bestiary. The Guild pays well for every one of them.
Ever since Hroggar's house burned, people have been whispering. Vampires, some say.
There used to be more of you. The war, and then, people just stopped coming back. Be careful out there.
liaisons.registerAsk: The Guild? Out here? Well, Morthal could certainly use the help. There's a small fee to join.

businessByRank.C: You've been busy out there, haven't you? Morthal notices. What is it?
businessByRank.B: Our veteran's back! The whole town's safer for it. What do you need?
businessByRank.A: Morthal's own hero, back at my counter. What can I do for you?
businessByRank.S: An S-rank, in Morthal. I never thought I'd see the day. What can I do for you?

liaisons.replace: Lost in the marsh, I'd wager. Half of Morthal's belongings are. Here's a new card.

liaisons.register: There, you're in. Here's your guild card. Nobody sleeps in Dawnstar lately anyway, might as well work.
liaisons.business: Guild business at this hour? Not like anyone's sleeping. Go on.
liaisons.promoteAsk: Karita, fetch the lamp. Well, look at that. You've earned your next rank. Pay the fee and I'll mark it down.
liaisons.promote: Congratulations. Your guild card's updated. Maybe now you'll sleep better than the rest of us.
about: The Pale's all ice and mines and giants. Miners post more work than anyone.
And the nightmares. Everyone in town's having them. If the Guild can fix that, I'll pay the bounty myself.
Fewer adventurers every year. The wars, and worse. Glad you're here.
liaisons.registerAsk: Joining the Guild? Good. Dawnstar needs all the help it can get. Just the fee, and you're in.

businessByRank.C: You've done good work around here. Karita's even written a verse about it. What is it?
businessByRank.B: A veteran, here in Dawnstar. The miners will be glad to hear it. Go on.
businessByRank.A: One of the Guild's best, in Dawnstar. The Pale's lucky to have you. Go on.
businessByRank.S: An S-rank. At my counter. Nobody in Dawnstar's going to believe me. What do you need?

afterQuest._comment: Waking Nightmare (Vaermina's nightmares on Dawnstar): once it is completed, these replace the lines that talk about them.
afterQuest.business: Guild business? Go on. Now that the nightmares are over, I can actually keep my eyes open for it.
afterQuest.register: There, you're in. Here's your guild card. The Pale always has work for a steady blade.
afterQuest.promote: Congratulations. Your guild card's updated. Drinks are on the house, now that we're all sleeping again.
about: The Pale's all ice and mines and giants. Miners post more work than anyone.
The nightmares are over, thank the gods. Now it's just the giants and the cold.
Fewer adventurers every year. The wars, and worse. Glad you're here.

liaisons.replace: Lost your card? It happens. Here's a new one, and the ledger still knows your name.

liaisons.register: Welcome to the Guild! Your card. The counter's the only thing in Winterhold still standing that isn't the College.
liaisons.business: Guild business. Most of it comes from the College, mages who won't leave their tower.
liaisons.promoteAsk: Haran, where did we put that book? Ah, you've earned a promotion! The Guild just wants its fee first.
liaisons.promote: Congratulations! Your guild card's updated. Most exciting thing to happen here since the Collapse.
about: Winterhold was a great city once, before the Collapse. Now it's the College and my inn.
Mages post the strangest missives. Ice wraith teeth, frost salts, things from the ruins.
The Guild's not what it was before the war. It could be again, with the right people.
liaisons.registerAsk: Want to join the Guild? Winterhold could use some excitement. There's a small fee to sign you up.

businessByRank.C: Back again? The mages keep asking whether you're free. What is it?
businessByRank.B: A veteran in Winterhold. Most exciting thing since the Collapse. What do you need?
businessByRank.A: One of the Guild's best, in Winterhold. The College keeps asking after you. What do you need?
businessByRank.S: An S-rank, here. Even the Arch-Mage will want to meet you. How can I be of service?

liaisons.replace: Lost your card? Things have a way of vanishing in Winterhold. Here's another, friend.

liaisons.register: I know everyone in Raven Rock, and they know me. Now they'll know you too. It's in the ledger. Take your guild card, adventurer.
liaisons.business: The end of the bar with the ledger on it is the Adventurers Guild. The other end is for drinking. Which end do you want?
liaisons.promoteAsk: Sit. I want to read this page properly. Azura knows I've poured for people who did less and bragged more. The Adventurers Guild takes its fee, and I get to write in the new letter.
liaisons.promote: There. I've changed the letter on your guild card. I've changed it in the story I tell about you, too.
about: Councilor Morvayn wouldn't hear of the Adventurers Guild for years. Then the ash spawn came over the Bulwark, and he sent Adril to my bar with a pen.
There's no missive board here. People with a problem tell their barkeep, and their barkeep tells an adventurer. It's an older system.
Names come over from Windhelm on the Northern Maiden. Adventurers the mainland says are on their way. I keep a second page for the ones who never walk through my door. It's longer than I'd like.
liaisons.registerAsk: You want to sign with the Adventurers Guild in Raven Rock? Most people who land here are trying to leave. I like you already, outlander. There's a fee. There's always a fee.

businessByRank.C: The Redoran Guard asked me who you were. I told them C-rank adventurer, and they stopped asking. What do you need?
businessByRank.B: Captain Veleth reads my ledger now, did you know? He stops at your page. B-rank. What'll it be?
businessByRank.A: I've started telling people an A-rank adventurer drinks here. It's good for business. Don't make a liar of me.
businessByRank.S: I've got a story about an S-rank adventurer who walked into my cornerclub. True story, friend. I'm still in the middle of it.

liaisons.replace: A lost guild card always comes with a story, and I collect those. No? Then it's the fee, and I'll make one up for you.

_staff: Other people who work at a guild inn point you to their rep. whileAlive / whenDead = an NPC editor ID the line needs alive / dead (the innkeeper it names; their successor). unlessInFaction {ref, faction} = the line is skipped while that reference is in that faction (Mikael's 'I got the inn' line, if Ysolda is the innkeeper after all).

staff.line: Guild business goes through Hulda. She's the Guild's rep here.
I got the inn, but Ysolda got the Guild gig. Go find her if you have Guild business.
Guild business goes through Ysolda now. She took the counter over when Hulda passed.
My father runs the Guild's counter. Talk to him.
Keerava handles anything to do with the Guild.
Guild? Talk to my husband. That's his business, not mine.
My father keeps the Guild's counter. I just sing.
The Adventurers Guild? That was Kleppr's ledger, not mine. I've an inn to run on my own now. Try the counter in another hold.
Father kept the Adventurers Guild's counter. I'm working on my certification, I am. One day this will be the finest counter in Skyrim. Until then, you'll want another hold.
Dagur kept the Adventurers Guild's ledger. I can pour your mead and rent you a bed, but the counter closed with him.
Jonna kept the Adventurers Guild's counter. There's no one to keep it now. I could sing you something about it?
Valga handled the Adventurers Guild's business. With her gone there's no counter in Falkreath. You'll have to ride to another hold.

_referrals: Innkeepers outside the hold capitals: no counter, but they know where to send you.

referrals.line: Guild business goes to the Bannered Mare in Whiterun. Hulda's the Guild's rep. Half a day north.
I just run an inn. Try the Bannered Mare in Whiterun.
Ivarstead's too small for a Guild counter. Try the Bee and Barb in Riften.
Rorikstead's a farming town. For the Guild you want the Bannered Mare in Whiterun.
The Winking Skeever in Solitude handles Guild business. Just follow the road across the bridge.
You want Windhelm for that. Candlelight Hall keeps the Guild's counter.
Nightgate's a waystation, friend, not a Guild house. Windhelm's your best bet.
No Guild counter out here. The Silver-Blood Inn in Markarth is closest.
The Guild keeps its counter at Candlelight Hall. Nords prefer their business kept among Nords.

_generic: Any other innkeeper, including ones added by other mods (anyone in JobInnkeeperFaction), unless they are travelling with the player as a follower.
generic: The Adventurers Guild keeps its counters in the hold capitals, near the missive boards. You won't find one out here.

prompts.register: I'd like to register with the Adventurers Guild.
prompts.promote: I'd like to apply for promotion.
prompts.about: What's Guild work like around here?
prompts.replace: I've lost my guild card. I need a replacement.

_nofee: What a guild liaison says when the player picks register/promote without the fee in hand (no Goodbye; voiced per liaison voice type).

nofee.register: Joining the Guild takes a small fee. Come back when you can cover it.
nofee.promote: You've earned it, no question. But the Guild still wants its fee. Come back with the coin.
nofee.replace: A new card costs coin. Come back when you can cover it.

_ask: The liaison names the fee before registering / promoting; the player then chooses to pay or not (voiced per liaison voice type). A liaison's own "<role>Ask" line (promoteAsk: checks the ledger, congratulates, then the fee) replaces this for them; their "<role>" line is then what they say once paid.

ask.register: There's a small fee to join the Adventurers Guild. Will you pay it?
ask.promote: The Guild charges a fee to see a promotion through. Will you pay it?

later.register: Suit yourself. The Guild will be here when you're ready.
later.promote: As you like. The rank will be waiting for you.
